q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) AS NEW FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) A WHERE NEW = (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT(PRODUCT_KEY) ORDER BY PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 checks if a customer has all distinct products by comparing the count of distinct products per customer to the total count of distinct products in the PRODUCT table. Q2 uses GROUP_CONCAT to compare the full ordered list of distinct product keys for each customer with the full ordered list from the PRODUCT table, which is more precise but not equivalent to Q1's approach in all cases.
